baseline_sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.segment,
    (
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM orders o
        WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id
          AND o.status = 'delivered'
    ) AS delivered_orders
FROM customers c
WHERE c.country = 'India'
LIMIT 100;
optimized_sql:
WITH delivered_counts AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.segment,
    COALESCE(dc.delivered_orders, 0) AS delivered_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN delivered_counts dc ON dc.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.country = 'India'
LIMIT 100;
verdict_summary: Measured execution time improved by 96.7% (201.321 ms -> 6.621 ms, 30.41x faster).

    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_date,
    o.total_amount
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.email LIKE '%example.com'
ORDER BY o.order_date DESC, o.order_id DESC
OFFSET 15000
LIMIT 50;
optimized_sql:
SELECT
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_date,
    o.total_amount
FROM orders o

WHERE c.email LIKE 'customer1%'
  AND (o.order_date, o.order_id) < (TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-09-01 00:00:00+00', 40000)

LIMIT 50;

baseline_sql:

    order_id,

    order_date,

ORDER BY order_date DESC

optimized_sql:
SELECT
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    order_date,
    total_amount
FROM orders
WHERE order_date >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-01-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND order_date < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY order_date DESC
LIMIT 200;
